html:
The Battle of Mohi was fought on 11 April 1241 at the Sajó River in northeastern Hungary, where a Mongol army under Batu and Subutai destroyed the army of King Béla IV.

The Mongols seized the bridge, surrounded the Hungarian camp and left a gap through which the fleeing army was cut down. The Mongols then ravaged the plains for a year, and a large part of the population died from killing and famine. Béla fled to the Adriatic coast. The Mongols left in 1242, probably because of the death of the Great Khan Ögedei. Béla rebuilt the country with stone castles and new settlers, and is called the second founder of the state. The same campaign had crushed the Poles at Legnica two days earlier. The Golden Bull had been issued under Béla's father.
sum: The Battle of Mohi was fought on 11 April 1241 at the Sajó River in northeastern Hungary, where a Mongol army under Batu and Subutai destroyed the army of King Béla IV.
